title: A specified scalar presentation gives the same coefficient-sheaf cokernel
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Lambda(*)$, and let $U$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $\Lambda_U$ for the pulled-back coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $Q$ put $E_U(Q)=\Lambda_U\otimes_{R_U}Q_U$, using the constant module sheaf and the canonical scalar map $R_U\to\Lambda_U$ of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Finite free modules and cokernels are taken in the module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Let $m,n\geq0$, let $A=(a_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq n,1\leq j\leq m}$ be a matrix over $R$, and let $q:R^n\to P$ exhibit $P$ as the cokernel of $A:R^m\to R^n$. Under the canonical identifications $E_U(R^r)\cong\Lambda_U^r$ the diagram $\Lambda_U^m\xrightarrow{A_U}\Lambda_U^n\xrightarrow{E_U(q)}E_U(P)$ is a cokernel diagram, where $A_U$ has entries the images of the very same $a_{ij}$ under $R\to\Gamma(U,\Lambda_U)$. In particular $E_U(P)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_U)$ for this specified presentation.

proof.text: Put $S=\Lambda_U$, and write $\varphi:R_U\to S$ for the given scalar map. Work on the small skeleton of $U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ in the coefficient universe specified by the site convention. Abelian sheaves there have the exact sheafification and closed sheafified tensor structure of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Thus [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies to both $R_U$ and $S$. Its equivalences preserve underlying sheaves and sections. By [def-sfb-modobj-extension], $E_U(Q)$ is the coequalizer of $(\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi))\otimes Q_U$ and $(S\otimes\gamma_{Q_U})\alpha$. Restrict $S$ along $\varphi$, with action $\gamma=\mu_S(\varphi\otimes S)$. Since $S$ is commutative [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], naturality of the braiding gives $\gamma\beta_{S,R_U}=\mu_S\beta_{S,S}(S\otimes\varphi)=\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi)$. Hence the two parallel pairs of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] and [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] are equal, and $E_U(Q)$ is the relative tensor $S\otimes_{R_U}Q_U$, with $S$ acting on the first factor. The pure-tensor comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], applied over $R_U$ to this restricted $S$ and $Q_U$, identifies that internal relative tensor with the sheafified sectionwise tensor. The comparison also respects the $S$-action: both actions send $t\cdot(s\otimes x)$ to $(ts)\otimes x$. Consequently we can compute $E_U$ in sectionwise module sheaves, and transfer the resulting diagrams back by these equivalences. Equivalences preserve a cokernel's factorization and uniqueness properties by their bijections on morphisms.

source.place: Tags 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); internal/sectionwise comparison uses Sites Tag 00YV

proof.text: Let $c(Q)=Q_U$. The constant presheaf diagram $R^m\xrightarrow{A}R^n\xrightarrow{q}P$ is a cokernel diagram in module presheaves. Indeed a natural map from the constant $R^n$ presheaf killing $A$ factors at each object uniquely through $q$; uniqueness forces these factors to commute with restrictions. The constant presheaf of $R^r$ is likewise the finite coproduct of $r$ constant $R$ presheaves. Apply the module sheafification $b$ of [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification]. Since $b$ is a left adjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] preserves these finite colimits, including the zero object and the coequalizer of $(A,0)$. Hence $c(q)$ exhibits $P_U$ as the cokernel of $c(A)$ and the induced identifications $c(R^r)\cong R_U^r$ preserve every standard basis section. On those sections $c(A)$ is still $e_j\mapsto\sum_i a_{ij}e_i$, with each coefficient now its constant section.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the identity geometric morphism of this topos, with ring map $\varphi:R_U\to S$. It states that the actual tensor functor $T=S\otimes_{R_U}-$ is left adjoint to restriction of scalars. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $T$ preserves the zero object, finite coproducts, and the coequalizer expressing the cokernel in step 2. Tensoring a zero map is zero by the defining tensor map on pure tensors. Therefore $E_U(q)=T(c(q))$ is a cokernel of $E_U(A)=T(c(A))$. This applies to the specified arrow $q$, not merely to a chosen abstract object isomorphic to $P$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), or the identity-topos specialization of Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); Categories Tag 0038

proof.text: Here is the normalization of the free-module identifications. After $c(R^r)\cong R_U^r$, define $\theta_r:S\otimes_{R_U}R_U^r\to S^r$ by $s\otimes(v_i)_i\mapsto(s\varphi(v_i))_i$ on sections. This pairing is balanced and natural under restriction, so [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] extends it to the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The inverse sends $(s_i)_i$ to $\sum_i s_i\otimes e_i$. One composite is the identity coordinatewise; the other sends $s\otimes v$ to $\sum_i s\varphi(v_i)\otimes e_i=\sum_i s\otimes v_i e_i=s\otimes v$, by balancing. The tensor universal property then gives equality of the sheaf maps. These maps are $S$-linear. Thus $\theta_r$ is the canonical isomorphism $E_U(R^r)\cong S^r$ sending $1\otimes e_j$ to $e_j$. For $r=0$ both maps are the unique maps between zero objects, and the same empty-sum calculation applies.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), balanced bilinear universal property after Tag 0GMW; explicit finite-free calculation

proof.text:
For each $j$, functoriality of the tensor construction and step 2 give
$\theta_n E_U(A)\theta_m^{-1}(e_j)=\theta_n(1\otimes\sum_i a_{ij}e_i)=\sum_i\varphi(a_{ij})e_i$.
Here $a_{ij}$ inside the tensor denotes its constant section. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], $\varphi(a_{ij})$ is precisely the image of the original scalar under $R\to\Gamma(U,\Lambda_U)$, and its restriction on every test object is used in this formula. A map out of the finite free sheaf is determined by the standard basis sections: any local section is $\sum_j s_j e_j$, and linearity fixes its image. Therefore $\theta_n E_U(A)\theta_m^{-1}=A_U$, with exactly the asserted entries and row/column convention.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), functorial map on pure tensors; blueprint det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model, scalar map in its opening paragraph

proof.text: Set $q_U=E_U(q)\theta_n^{-1}:S^n\to E_U(P)$. Steps 3 and 5 give $q_U A_U=0$. Given any $S$-linear $h:S^n\to N$ with $hA_U=0$, the map $h\theta_n:E_U(R^n)\to N$ kills $E_U(A)$, so step 3 gives a unique $k:E_U(P)\to N$ with $kE_U(q)=h\theta_n$. Equivalently $kq_U=h$. This is precisely the cokernel universal property of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Thus the specified diagram is a cokernel diagram. Applying the same property to a chosen $\operatorname{coker}(A_U)$ yields mutually inverse maps commuting with the quotient arrows; uniqueness proves the inverse identities. This gives the claimed canonical isomorphism $E_U(P)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_U)$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ and Section 03EK, conclusion by the cokernel universal property
